transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… hi. I’m Santiago. I guess what brings me in is this thing that’s been happening with food, mostly late at night. It’s not just that I snack or that I’m hungry, exactly. It’s more like I’ll start picking at something, and at first I’ll tell myself it’s no big deal, just a little bit, but then there’s this point where I’m saying in my head, “That’s enough, Santiago, stop now,” and my hand just keeps going back.

And that’s the part that worries me, honestly. It feels like I don’t really get to make the decision anymore once it starts. Like I know I should stop, I’m telling myself to stop, but I keep reaching for more anyway. That feeling of not being in control is what made me think maybe I should talk to someone.
When you find yourself continuing to eat even though you’re telling yourself to stop, do you notice yourself eating much faster or eating a lot more than you intended in a short amount of time?

Yeah… yes, I do. That’s actually one of the parts that feels strange when I think about it afterward. I’m not eating the way I would if I was sitting at the table with my family, you know, having dinner and talking and actually tasting things. It’s more… rushed. Like I’m trying to get through it before anyone notices, or before anyone wakes up.

I’ll be standing there, sometimes not even properly sitting down, and I’m just putting food in my mouth fast. Not really enjoying it, not really paying attention to flavor the way I normally would. It’s like the goal becomes finishing it, or getting it over with, which sounds weird because I’m the one choosing to eat it, but in the moment it doesn’t feel slow or normal. It feels hurried, almost like I’m racing against something.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah, it does distress me. I mean, I’m not falling apart in the obvious ways, I guess. I’m still going to work, still making it to my shipping and receiving shifts, still doing what I’m supposed to do there—checking things in, moving inventory around, keeping track of stuff. So from the outside I probably look like I’m functioning pretty normally.

But it’s there in the background, and it’s started changing how I act at home. Like later in the evening, when my family might still be in or around the kitchen, I’ve started avoiding that time a little bit. Not because I don’t want to be with them, exactly, but because I feel tense around the food and I’m worried they’ll notice I’m acting weird, or that I’m too focused on it. So I’ll hang back, or find a reason to be somewhere else, and then I feel bad about that too.

It’s not ruining every part of my life, but it’s definitely bothering me and making me feel… I don’t know, ashamed and on edge in my own house.
When you're having these episodes of eating, do you find yourself eating even when you're not really hungry, or continuing to eat until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah… a lot of the time I’m not really hungry when it starts. That’s one of the things that makes me feel so confused about it, because it’s not like I skipped dinner or I’m starving or something. Most nights I’ve already eaten dinner with everybody, like a normal meal, and I know I’m not physically hungry afterward.

But then later, when the house is quieter or I’m passing through the kitchen, I’ll still end up opening the fridge. Sometimes I’m just looking, like I’m telling myself I’m only checking what’s there, but then I start again. And in my head I know, “You already ate, you don’t need this,” but that doesn’t always stop me. It feels less like hunger and more like this pull to keep going back to the food anyway.
After these episodes of eating, do you find yourself feeling guilty, disgusted with yourself, or depressed about what you've eaten?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean… I know I don’t feel good about it afterward, but I don’t know if I’d use all those words every time. Sometimes I just feel kind of blank at first, like I don’t want to think about it too closely.

Then I’ll notice I’m uncomfortable with myself, like, “Why did I do that?” But I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, exactly. And disgusted sounds strong… maybe sometimes I get close to that, but I don’t really sit there naming it in my head. It’s more like I try to move on quickly, clean up whatever I used, and not have anyone notice.

So… I guess there’s some bad feeling afterward, but I’m not totally sure how to separate out guilt from embarrassment or just feeling disappointed in myself.
